config.text: Create `~/.ssh/config` so that `ssh srv` logs in as `{{user}}` on `192.168.1.10`. Then run `hostname` on the server with `ssh srv`.
config.hint: Three lines: `Host srv`, `    HostName 192.168.1.10` and `    User {{user}}`. Write them with `echo ... >> ~/.ssh/config` and then run `ssh srv hostname`.

scp-up.text: Copy `~/{{notes}}` to your home directory on the server with `scp`.
scp-up.hint: `scp ~/{{notes}} srv:` – the colon after `srv` means "on the server", and without a path the file ends up in the home directory there.

scp-down.text: Fetch the file `{{welcomeFile}}` from the home directory on the server to the directory `~/{{downloads}}`.
scp-down.hint: The source first, the target last: `scp srv:{{welcomeFile}} ~/{{downloads}}/`.

rsync-local.text: Back up the contents of `~/{{documents}}` to the directory `/tmp/{{documents}}` with `rsync -av`.
rsync-local.hint: The slash after the source means "what is in": `rsync -av ~/{{documents}}/ /tmp/{{documents}}`.

rsync-again.text: Create the file `~/{{documents}}/{{todo}}` and run the same `rsync -av` again. Only the new file should be sent.
rsync-again.hint: `touch ~/{{documents}}/{{todo}}` and then `rsync -av ~/{{documents}}/ /tmp/{{documents}}`. Without `-a`, everything is sent every time.

rsync-server.text: Sync the contents of `~/{{documents}}` to the directory `{{documents}}` in your home directory on the server.
rsync-server.hint: The same as before, but with the server as the target: `rsync -av ~/{{documents}}/ srv:{{documents}}/`.

dry-run.text: Remove `~/{{documents}}/{{todo}}` and then try `rsync -av --delete` to `/tmp/{{documents}}` with `-n` – so that you see what would be removed, without anything happening.
